public_rationale: There is evidence for rising training costs and a reported data bottleneck affecting Orion's coding performance. That does not establish that all major developers use effectively the same data or that this explains near-identical models. Anthropic's reported improvements at unchanged customer prices also complicate the claim. The broad causal conclusion remains unsettled.
limitations: The strongest specific support comes from reporting on anonymous sources.
Training costs, operating costs, and customer prices are different measures.
Company benchmarks do not independently establish real-world capability gains.

statement.excerpt: Instead, big tech has found itself peddling increasingly-more-expensive iterations of near-identical Large Language Models — a direct result of them all having to use the same training data, which it’s now running out of.

from_speaker: all having to use the same training data
our_interpretation: Assess the frontier-model development cycle discussed in 2024 through publication.
Read 'near-identical' as little meaningful difference in capabilities or useful behavior, not literally identical model weights.
The surrounding discussion primarily concerns development and operating costs; customer prices are a plausible alternative reading.
Read shared data as substantially overlapping usable training material. The causal claim requires evidence that limited data explains the cost and capability pattern.
'Running out' means a binding or worsening shortage of useful new data, not necessarily complete exhaustion.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable evidence shows rising costs and little meaningful capability improvement across the relevant developers, and identifies shared, increasingly scarce training data as a substantial cause.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable evidence shows substantial capability or cost improvements inconsistent with the claimed pattern, or establishes that the asserted shared-data bottleneck does not explain it.
